description: Render a quario report definition to one target and write the output to a file. Returns the file's absolute path, never its content. A definition with problems returns them instead, as validate_report does.

CellStyleDeclarations.description: What a table cell declares: the vocabulary less flow spacing. The same narrowing a slot takes, under its own name because the engine refuses the two in their own words and a reader follows the wording to the node.

currency.description: What this cell's money is denominated in, under `format: "currency"`: a three-letter ISO 4217 code, beating the instance's default. A literal that is not one is a definition error; an `=` result that is not one is the cell's own answer still, so the cell presents as display text rather than falling back to the instance's currency. Unread without the kind.

family.description: `'sans'` | `'serif'` | `'mono'`, or an embedded font family name.

format.description: How a number or date is presented: a kind, or an object naming one and carrying the modifiers that kind understands — `digits`, `negative` and `zero` for the three number kinds, `form` for `date`. Locale stays on the instance.

href.description: Where this cell's text points: a URL, or `#` and a group's `label` for a destination inside the document. The one declaration the engine judges rather than passes on — a URL is admitted against the instance's `schemes` allowlist before it crosses, and a refused value is omitted, so the text renders and the link does not. A table row refuses it.

uppercase.description: Render the text in capitals. Capitals, not small caps.

valign.description: Vertical alignment within a box taller than its content: a table cell or row, a split slot (text or image). A definition error on a stacked item and on a band image, whose boxes have no such slack.

CellValue.description: A cell value: one template string, or a non-empty array of styled runs. A cell written as one template string is one run, so a one-run array says exactly what that string says.

CurrencyCode.description: A three-letter ISO 4217 code, by shape.

DateForm.description: The four named date forms, Intl's own `dateStyle`. A `date` that names none is `"medium"`.

Expression.description: An `=` expression: xprsn source after the leading `=`.

FormatDeclaration.description: How an author writes `format`: the kind alone, or the kind carrying the modifiers it takes. `digits` is a whole number from 0 to 20 — the range both a presenting target and a worksheet number format can honour — and it beats the count the kind would otherwise present, a currency's minor units included. A modifier on a kind that does not take it is a definition error.

GridColumn.description: One column of a grid: the width share every row's slot in this position takes, and the declarations each of those slots layers its own over.

width.description: Column width as a percentage of the content width (0 < width <= 100).

GridItem.description: Splits that share one column geometry: the widths, and each column's style, are stated once and every row is laid on them. Every rule a split has, a row has — full content width, no nesting, never broken across a page — and each row crosses the event stream as the split bracket it is.

GridRow.description: One line on a grid's geometry: a split without `type`. A row naming fewer slots than the grid has columns leaves the rest empty, so `{}` is a spacer line of the row's size.

alt.description: The image's textual stand-in: one template string. A styled run means nothing on a stand-in for a picture, so this is the one cell value the widened type does not reach.

GridSlot.description: One slot of a grid row: a split slot less `width`, which the slot takes from its column.

break.description: Where this group turns a page (paginated targets). Every boundary between consecutive instances turns; `before` adds the run's leading edge, `after` its trailing edge, and `around` both.

collapsed.description: Open every instance of this group shut: its own header and footer show, and the content between them does not. A target with a way to hide a row and keep it -- the worksheet -- hides those rows, where a reader opens the group again. The rest drop them, and the [matrix](https://getquario.com/docs/reference/support-matrix) says which does which.

columns.description: Flow each instance's content in this many page columns (integer >= 2). Columned regions cannot nest.

instances.description: Order and cut this group's instances, as the group's own `sort` and `take` order and cut the rows inside each. Absent, every instance renders in first-seen order.

label.description: This instance's name for **navigation** rather than for the page: one template, resolved once per instance in group scope, where the handle and `$` are bound and `@` is unbound. A target with somewhere to put a navigation name spends it there and the rest withdraw it, so it never changes what the page shows.

reset.description: Restart `page.number` / `page.total` at every instance. It turns no page of its own, so it requires `break` to be `"before"` or `"around"`.

run.description: Running accumulators, read as `run.<name>` on detail rows.

take.description: Keep this many rows after this group's `sort`. Integer >= 1. Rows past the count are dropped from aggregates and runners, unlike `visible`.

ImageFit.description: How an image is sized: at its intrinsic size, or scaled to the content width.

ImageItem.description: A host-supplied graphic in the band flow. `source` is an expression (never a literal — JSON has no way to write bytes) yielding the complete image file as a `Uint8Array` of PNG, JPEG or SVG bytes; nullish skips the item silently, anything else invalid is a located render error.

alt.description: The image's textual stand-in: one template string. A styled run means nothing on a stand-in for a picture, so this is the one cell value the widened type does not reach.

ImageStyleDeclarations.description: The declarations an image item accepts: the box, plus the four names that are not about text. The rest of the vocabulary describes text, which an image does not have, so any other name on one is a definition error. A narrowing of the one vocabulary rather than a second list of its own, so the two cannot drift.

spaceAfter.description: Blank space after this item, in points.

spaceBefore.description: Blank space before this item, in points.

Instances.description: How a group orders and cuts its instances.

sort.description: Order the instances. Each key reads the group's own handle once per instance, with `@` and `run` unbound.

take.description: Keep this many instances after `sort`. Integer >= 1. A dropped instance never renders, so no runner steps over it, but the enclosing aggregates still count it.

Item.description: One item in a band: text, an image, a split, or a grid. Future types may be additive.

JsonValue.description: A value a JSON document can hold. `params` accepts these and nothing else: a Date, Map, Set or typed array is a definition error, as are `NaN` and `Infinity`, which this type cannot exclude but the traversal rejects.

LineStyle.description: The line a border side is drawn with.

NegativeReading.description: How a negative amount reads. A number kind that names none is `"minus"`.

Orientation.description: Which way the paper is turned.

PageBands.description: Page header/footer bands, rendered once per page by paginated targets (unpaginated targets ignore them). Cells read `$` and the `page` anchor (`page.number` / `page.total`, 1-based, the current sequence); `@` stays unbound.

margin.description: The inset from the paper's edge, in points: one number for all four sides, or each side named. Required when the report header declares `height`. A target's own `margin` option applies where this is absent, and declaring both is a render error.

orientation.description: Which way the paper is turned.

size.description: The report's paper, by name. A `[width, height]` pair is a target option only. A target's own `size` option applies where this is absent, and declaring both is a render error.

PageMargin.description: A margin that names each side, in points. All four are required.

PaperName.description: The named paper sizes a document may declare.

ParamDeclaration.description: What a report declares it needs. A bare value under `params` *is* the parameter's value; a plain object is a declaration. `default` absent means the parameter is required, and a render that supplies none is rejected before any expression runs. `type` names a JSON kind, because a parameter is a JSON value. A `null` default beside a `type` makes the parameter optional and lets a render supply `null`.

label.description: The text a person reads for this parameter. A parameter with a label is one a person supplies; the engine never renders it.

ParamValue.description: A parameter's value when it is not a declaration: any JSON value but a plain object, which `params` reads as a declaration.

ReportStyleDeclarations.description: What a report default declares: the two declarations a typeface is made of. Anything else is a definition error, as on an image item.

family.description: `'sans'` | `'serif'` | `'mono'`, or an embedded font family name.

RowStyleDeclarations.description: What a row box declares: a cell's names less the three that present a value. A box wraps cells and holds no value of its own, so `format`, `currency` and `href` have nothing to act on. Worn by the detail row, the header row's box and both halves of the totals block.

family.description: `'sans'` | `'serif'` | `'mono'`, or an embedded font family name.

uppercase.description: Render the text in capitals. Capitals, not small caps.

valign.description: Vertical alignment within a box taller than its content: a table cell or row, a split slot (text or image). A definition error on a stacked item and on a band image, whose boxes have no such slack.

RunStyleDeclarations.description: The declarations a styled run accepts: the inline half of the vocabulary, and nothing else. The box and flow spacing describe a block and `align` describes a line, and neither means anything on part of one — so a run is narrowed from the other end than an image item is. A narrowing of the one vocabulary rather than a second list of its own, so the two cannot drift.

SlotImageStyleDeclarations.description: What an image slot declares: an image item's names less flow spacing, plus `valign` — the one name an image accepts in a slot and nowhere else, because a slot's box is the split's height rather than the picture's own.

valign.description: Vertical alignment within a box taller than its content: a table cell or row, a split slot (text or image). A definition error on a stacked item and on a band image, whose boxes have no such slack.

SlotStyleDeclarations.description: What a text slot declares: the vocabulary less flow spacing, which is a band-item pad and does not apply inside a split.

SplitItem.description: Items placed across the content width rather than stacked down the band — the invoice header's "seller left, customer right". A split is always the full content width and never nests; a slot that renders nothing keeps its width, so the line's geometry does not move with the data.

width.description: Slot width as a percentage of the content width (0 < width <= 100).

alt.description: The image's textual stand-in: one template string. A styled run means nothing on a stand-in for a picture, so this is the one cell value the widened type does not reach.

width.description: Slot width as a percentage of the content width (0 < width <= 100).

SplitSlot.description: One slot of a split: an ordinary item, plus the width share that is a slot property rather than an item one. A split may not stand in a slot — placement inside placement is the coordinate system quario does not have.

StackedStyleDeclarations.description: What a stacked item declares: the vocabulary less `valign`. A stacked item sits in a band's flow and its box is its own height, so there is nothing for it to align against — where a slot's box is the split's height, which is why a slot keeps the name.

currency.description: What this cell's money is denominated in, under `format: "currency"`: a three-letter ISO 4217 code, beating the instance's default. A literal that is not one is a definition error; an `=` result that is not one is the cell's own answer still, so the cell presents as display text rather than falling back to the instance's currency. Unread without the kind.

spaceAfter.description: Blank space after this item, in points.

spaceBefore.description: Blank space before this item, in points.

uppercase.description: Render the text in capitals. Capitals, not small caps.

StyleDeclarations.description: The closed, target-neutral style vocabulary. Literal values are validated strictly (unknown names and mistyped literals are definition errors); `=` expression results are coerced leniently by each target at render. Colors are `#rgb`/`#rrggbb` hex only. Each target maps the declarations to its own formatting model (the HTML target to inline CSS, the PDF target to faces, points, and rects).

currency.description: What this cell's money is denominated in, under `format: "currency"`: a three-letter ISO 4217 code, beating the instance's default. StyledRun.description: One styled run: a stretch of a cell's text with its own declarations. A closed two-key object — `{{#if}}` already conditions a run's own text, so there is no `visible` on one.

header.description: Absent exactly when a neighbour's header `span` covers this column: every column's header slot is filled once, by its own or by a span.

width.description: Column width as a percentage of the table width (0 < width <= 100).

span.description: How many columns this header covers — a literal integer >= 1, never an expression; absent is 1. The columns it covers omit their own `header`.

TableHeaderBox.description: The header row's own box — distinct from `TableHeader`, which is one column's header cell. This is the box the row wears, replayed with the header cells on every page continuation.

TotalBlock.description: The table's summary block: the rows, plus what belongs to the block rather than to any one of them. Its `style` is the layer below each row's — box under box, everything else under everything else — and exact `false` on its `visible` omits the block whole, its rows never evaluated.

TotalCell.description: One cell of a total row: an ordinary cell, plus the columns it covers. The spans in a row must sum to the column count exactly.

span.description: How many columns this cell covers — a literal integer >= 1, never an expression; absent is 1.

WidthShare.description: A share of the width, in percent.

ZeroReading.description: How a zero reads. A number kind that names none is `"number"`.

currency.description: The default currency code for `format: "currency"`, for this render.

data.description: The render data, any JSON value. Give exactly one of `data` and `dataPath`. An object whose only key is `$image` or `$base64` decodes to bytes, which is how an image's `source` expression reads a picture. `{ "$image": "assets/logo.png" }` names a PNG or JPEG inside the server's data root, and costs far less context than `{ "$base64": "…" }`.

dataPath.description: A JSON file holding the render data, as a path inside the server's data root. `$image` and `$base64` objects decode there too, and an `$image` path resolves against the data root, not the file.

definition.description: The report definition to check or render.

$schema.description: Where an editor finds this document's JSON Schema. The engine checks that it is a string and reads nothing else.

columns.description: Flow the report body in this many page columns (integer >= 2). Columned regions cannot nest.

header.description: Dual-shaped like `detail`: an item array, or `{ height, items }` when the header pins a flow box from the page top.

required.description: The declarations this document cannot do without, each marked `true`. Only [`plan`](https://getquario.com/docs/diving-deeper/validating) reads it, against the target descriptors its caller names: every required declaration one of them withdraws or leaves unread becomes a problem of its own at `required.<name>`, which nulls the report as any other problem does. No target sees the marking, and no render changes because of it.

run.description: Running accumulators, read as `run.<name>` on detail rows.

style.description: The report default: the typeface this document is set in. It sits under the targets' band-role defaults and under every item's own `style`, so a declared `size` does not change a report header's headline size.

take.description: Keep this many rows after the report `sort`. Integer >= 1. Rows past the count are dropped from aggregates and runners, unlike `visible`.

filename.description: The basename to write under, without a directory. The target's extension is forced, and a name that exists is never overwritten. Omit it for `report-<timestamp>`.

locale.description: The locale `format` presents in, for this render.

options.description: Options for the target: `page` and `meta` for pdf, xlsx and docx, and `filter` for xlsx. The csv target takes none.

filter.description: xlsx: an autofilter over each worksheet's one table.

meta.description: Document properties: `title`, `author` and `subject`, each a string.

page.description: Page geometry: `size`, `margin`, and for xlsx `orientation` and `fit`.

timeZone.description: The time zone dates present in, for this render.
